contents: The center: four thrusts, one loop
September at the center, and what comes next

letter.title: Finished work, and the people behind it
paragraphs: Welcome to the second issue. September brought four new papers. Yan Luo's group, with Christopher Niezrecki and Murat Inalpolat, built a sensor network that listens to wind turbine blades to check their structural health. Arash Rezaee and Ryan McCann published FUSION, the open-source optical networking platform from our first issue's student story. Yuanchang Xie's group studied how drivers merge near work-zone signs. And Negin Yazdani Motlagh studied what computing employers ask for in job posts; her story is inside.

Our faculty spotlight is Lewis Tseng, who works on keeping groups of computers in agreement when some of them fail or are attacked. In August he won an NSF award to plan a shared data system for microscopy. Two of his four Ph.D. students are in the School of Education, co-advised with Mark Hsu, and that is the kind of collaboration we want more of.

On October 1, NSF's SUMMIT award began, and we are hiring a postdoctoral researcher to help build it. If you know someone who should apply, or a company that wants to test equipment against a real-time model of the Northeast grid, the last page says how to reach us.
